articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert responded to a fan that called out his three-point shooting following the team's 127-125 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday.

After a fan posted a video on social media in which he told Gobert to "not shoot another motherf--king set of threes" as long as he plays for the Timberwolves, the three-time All-Star replied with a comment.

"What you gonna do about it?" Gobert wrote.

Ant's Injury Doesn't Worry Wolves' President

Gobert attempted two three-pointers during Minnesota's overtime defeat at the hands of Cleveland, missing both of them.

He grabbed 20 rebounds in the contest, but scored just five points on 0-of-9 shooting.

Gobert has established himself as an elite rim protector throughout his career, earning four Defensive Player of the Year awards. His offensive approach has traditionally been limited to layups and dunks, though.

The 34-year-old has attempted 24 triples across his 14 seasons in the NBA, but has yet to connect on one. Gobert's inaccuracy from behind the arc isn't a major surprise, as he also shoots just 63.3 percent on free throws.

Still, it seems like he plans to continue trying to expand his range as the Timberwolves look to clinch a sixth consecutive playoff appearance.

articles.title: Attorney compares SEC commissioner Greg Sankey to ‘Kim Jong’ in LSU-RJ Luis eligibility lawsuit
articles.summary: RJ Luis' injunction gives the LSU Tigers legal cover to roster him this season, but the SEC's threats could push the case toward monetary damages.
articles.body: The ongoing legal battle between the LSU Tigers and the Southeastern Conference took another turn on Wednesday afternoon inside the same courthouse that has drawn plenty of attention over the past two months. Former St. John's basketball player RJ Luis has been fighting to play this season for Will Wade and the Tigers, but SEC rules prohibit him from taking the court for LSU due to him signing an NBA contract or having professional experience. At first, Luis was granted the ability to participate in the upcoming season thanks to an order granted by a Louisiana judge based off a lawsuit filed against the NCAA over its eligibility rules pertaining to the members of the 2022 class who felt as though they should have been enjoined with new guidelines established. MAHJONG IS THE NEW TAILGATE GAME TAKING OVER COLLEGE FOOTBALL FOR WOMEN — AND EVEN AT HOME WITH HEAD COACHES Now, thanks to an injunction granted by a Louisiana judge, RJ Luis has provided LSU with protection to roster him this season if they have the fortitude to continue battling the SEC. The latest injunction granted allows Luis to practice and play with LSU until a Nov. 13 hearing in Baton Rouge, allowing LSU the legal power needed for the Tigers to roster RJ Luis without facing penalties from the SEC. But, will LSU follow the court's ruling? Remember those athletes Lane Kiffin thought about rostering at LSU? During the time between the order being granted and Wednesday, there has been another case that saw both the SEC and LSU added to a lawsuit that pertained to the eligibility of athletes. As OutKick previously reported, a judge in the 19th Judicial District Court of Baton Rouge granted an injunction for former athletes that had NFL 'experience' in Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. It was at the injunction hearing for those two athletes where SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey was called to the witness stand, testifying for over three hours on the Thursday before LSU opened the season against Clemson. INSIDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN Thanks to a ruling by Judge William Jorden in the favor of the athletes, both players were eligible to be rostered by Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers without punishment from the SEC. But, the threat of recourse by the conference, along with a federal lawsuit filed by the SEC that very same week, saw the LSU athletic department make the decision to keep them off the team. LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN Now, nearly two months later, LSU basketball coach Will Wade technically has the same decision to make. Will LSU roster RJ Luis? Attorney compares Greg Sankey to Kim Jong Un in latest shot After Will Wade noted that he would be following SEC guidelines pertaining to former professional athletes not being added to the official roster, he now faces another decision that should not be that difficult to make, unless he's worried about being sued. Attorney Tony Clayton, who is also part of the legal team for Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, told reporters outside the Baton Rouge courthouse on Wednesday that since he added both the conference and LSU to the amended complaint, it provides his client with a path to play this season despite what the SEC guidelines say. "My client, Mr. Luis, felt that it was in his best interest to file this claim against LSU and the SEC because of the commissioner's actions and the commissioner's threat," attorney Tony Clayton told NOLA.com, "LSU may be intimidated by ‘Kim Jong’ Sankey, but we're not." Okay, that's not going to sit well with the conference, as they continue fighting LSU in federal court, in a separate case. Does RJ Luis actually think he will be rostered by Will Wade this season? Well, attorney Tony Clayton pointed out why in his legal filing he brought LSU into this fight, and why he thinks this provides the Tigers with cover from conference rules. "The reason why we brought LSU into the suit is because LSU is being threatened by Mr. Sankey," Clayton told NOLA.com. "LSU is a great institution. Coach Wade is a good guy, a good coach, but both of them need to be forced to allow RJ to play basketball since he's obviously qualified. And not have the threat of the SEC, which is threatening LSU. In effect, stopping coach Will Wade from letting this kid exercise his fundamental right to play basketball." But, if you've been paying close attention to what has taken place over the past two months, this might actually come down to monetary damages, and not RJ Luis playing basketball for LSU this season. According to multiple sources, attorneys for the two former football players could end up bringing a civil suit against the SEC over the coming weeks that seeks damages for them not being rostered by Lane Kiffin and LSU. In their eyes, it's the SEC's threat of action against LSU if they were to roster these athletes that prevented them from playing this season. So, could the injunction granted to RJ Luis on Wednesday, which remains in effect until a Nov. 13 hearing, be the next step in the former St. John's basketball star's lawsuit against the SEC as he seeks monetary damages? Or, maybe a settlement with all athletes somehow tied to LSU in these cases. Not even a long game that plays out inside courtrooms from Alabama to Baton Rouge.

articles.title: Bam Adebayo shakes off 'scapegoat' label, leads Heat past Hawks for first win of the season after 0-4 start
articles.summary: Bam Adebayo dropped a season-high 24 points to lift the Heat to a 129-117 win over the Hawks on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Bam Adebayo seems to have found his shot.

The Miami Heat star, days after saying he felt like the team's "scapegoat" amid their losing streak, led the franchise to their first win of the new season on Wednesday night. He dropped a season-high 24 points while shooting 8 of 16 from the field to carry the Heat to a 129-117 win over the Atlanta Hawks at the State Farm Arena, which ended their four-game losing skid.

Adebayo had nine rebounds, too, which brought him to 5,794 in his career. That broke Udonis Haslem's all-time franchise record.

The Heat led for most of the first half, after a bit of back-and-forth to start, and took a 13-point lead into the locker room — thanks in part to a wild half-court buzzer-beater from Nikola Jović, who looked just as stunned as everyone else inside State Farm Arena.

Adebayo had 13 of his 24 points in the first half while shooting 5 of 9 from the field.

The Heat didn't let up in the third quarter, and Adebayo added nine more to keep their lead at 12. They were up by 18 at one point, but the Hawks closed the half on a 7-2 run in about 90 seconds, capped by an Andrew Wiggins 3-pointer in the final moments of the period.

Though the Hawks cut it to just four points midway through the fourth quarter, that was as close as they got. The Heat responded with seven straight points to take control of the contest and secure the 12-point win.

Giannis Antetokounmpo, who had a triple-double in the loss on Monday, finished with 24 points and 18 rebounds in the win for the Heat. Andrew Wiggins added 18 points. The Heat ended up shooting 53% from the field.

Nickeil Alexander-Walker led the Hawks with 23 points while draining five from behind the arc. Rookie Kingston Flemings added 23 points off the bench, and CJ McCollum finished with 13 points. The Hawks have lost three straight and now sit at 2-3 on the season.

While it was only four games, the Heat's winless start to the season led to plenty of questions about the franchise that made a blockbuster move to bring in Antetokounmpo this past offseason. Adebayo looked, well, rough in the first stretch of the season, too. He averaged just 11.8 points and 7.3 rebounds per contest over the first four games, all well down from his numbers last season. Adebayo even had an 83-point outing back in March .

After their loss to the Mavericks on Monday night, he said he felt like the "scapegoat" and was getting all of the blame for the team's struggles.

"You know, it's funny how the outside noise wants to make me the scapegoat," he said on Monday. "But when the tables turn, just all that energy, when the energy shifts, just be prepared for that."

As it turns out, it didn't take long for the energy to shift. Adebayo had his best game of the season just 48 hours later, and the Heat now have a tick in the win column.

articles.title: Trade Packages and Landing Spots for New Orleans Pelicans' Herb Jones
articles.summary: Expectations weren't high for the New Orleans Pelicans coming into this season. And yet, after their 0-3 start, it feels like they're performing below them.
articles.body:
Expectations weren't high for the New Orleans Pelicans coming into this season. And yet, after their 0-3 start, it feels like they're performing below them.

The Pelicans have had second-half leads in all three of those losses. They were up 23 in the second half against the Denver Nuggets. And while teams have been surging by them in high-leverage moments, the coaching staff has been unwilling to embrace Herb Jones' defense as a way to slow them down.

Jones is playing a career-low 17.0 minutes per game, and that has the rumor mill churning. In the N.O.'s Shamit Dua shared the latest:

"Multiple league sources indicate teams are monitoring Jones' situation and could pursue him if the Pelicans asking price changes. A recent video of Jones and Dumars speaking at practice has added to the speculation about his future.

"League sources say the Pelicans have held firm at an asking price near two first-round picks, though no team has met that figure. Many in the league believe Jones' value will continue to go down if his minutes continue to be sporadic. Jones' contract is also slated to jump next year from $14.9 million to $20.8 million. Nevertheless, several playoff teams view Jones as a valuable cultural and basketball fit.

"...The Pelicans...continue to rebuff offers, which have mostly been based around second round picks."

On the one hand, two first-round picks for Jones is too much of an ask. On the other, it's not hard to understand New Orleans passing on deals built around second-rounders. Surely, there's a happy medium.

And below, we'll give you exactly that (as well as a trade that might meet the Pelicans' current asking price and another that's more along the lines of the offers New Orleans has already received).

NOLA's Asking Price of 'Near Two First-Round Picks' (the Overpay)

Pelicans Receive: A 2027 first-round pick (via Denver, if No. 6 through No. 30) and a top-eight protected 2030 first-round pick

The Oklahoma City Thunder, with all the young talent they already have and the size of their treasure chest of future draft assets, are one of the few teams that could justify meeting New Orleans' reported asking price.

They'll barely see a dent in their trove of picks, and this will make it easier to sign the second contracts of young players like Aday Mara, Bennett Stirtz, Jared McCain, Nikola Topić and Thomas Sorber.

OKC also has a big enough trade exception to absorb all of Jones' $14.9 million salary. And while that will put them into the second apron, potentially season-ending injuries to Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace could make them desperate enough to go there (it could also motivate a gap year, but we won't entertain that here).

The Thunder suddenly need some wing depth. And even if Jones' three-point percentage doesn't bounce back to where it was in 2023-24 (when he was at 41.8 percent from deep), his perimeter defense would make him an instant culture fit in OKC.

For New Orleans, the thinking here is obvious. This actually exceeds the asking price of near two first-round picks, even if both are likely to be outside the lottery.

Turning a player currently on the fringe of the rotation into two future assets, while opening up some developmental minutes for younger players, makes plenty of sense for the Pelicans.

'Based Around Second-Round Picks' (the Underpay)

Pelicans Receive: Terance Mann, a 2030 second-round pick (via Lakers), a 2031 second-round pick and a 2032 second-round pick

Part of the motivation for New Orleans on this one would be the increased financial flexibility it'd have with Terance Mann. His deal expires two years earlier than Jones'. Having him as an expiring contract next season could make him a good trade piece in 2027-28, too.

That may not be enough to overcome the lack of first-rounders in this deal, but Brooklyn's stash of second-rounders is massive. Depending on how protections shake out, they could have up to 18 tradable seconds between now and 2033. That makes it a lot easier for them to justify giving up three (or maybe even four).

And Jones is the kind of wing that would both fit with the Nets and potentially be worth that many late picks.

Brooklyn has a decent offensive foundation with Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and several young playmakers with a chance to become impact players on that end, but it's woefully short on defense. Adding Jones would go a long way toward checking that box.

Pelicans Receive: Kristaps Porziņģis, a lottery-protected 2027 first-round pick and a 2032 second-round pick (if No. 31 through No. 50)

Two firsts does indeed feel a little rich for Jones. But in the right situation, he could be worth one protected first-rounder. And if the Pelicans still drag their feet, the Golden State Warriors should be OK with tossing in a second-round sweetener.

This is exactly the kind of situation where Jones could thrive. His perimeter defense could go a long way toward covering for Stephen Curry's struggles on that end. And Curry's gravity as a shooter and offensive engine could pull defenses away from Jones and give him a better shot at recreating his prior shooting success.

Adding Jones' three-and-D potential to a core that includes Curry, Yaxel Lendeborg and (hopefully) Jimmy Butler at some later point this season is worth two middling picks and a player who isn't likely to see the floor this season (Kristaps Porziņģis' health has put his career in question, and his contract was essentially designed to make him a human trade exception for 2026-27).

As for the Pelicans, this comes up a little short of the asking price, but it's hard to see anyone getting there, especially with the coaching staff failing to showcase Jones right now.

This package still gives New Orleans more financial flexibility (Jones' contract runs through 2029-30, while KP's is only guaranteed for $3 million next season) and a good shot at another first-rounder in 2027.

articles.title: 'F--k Development,' Warriors Insider Explains Yaxel Lendeborg's Opportunities vs. Jonathan Kuminga
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg is just four games into his NBA career, but already looks like a star in the making.
articles.body:
Yaxel Lendeborg is just four games into his NBA career, but already looks like a star in the making.

It's a rare sight for the Golden State Warriors, who haven't had much success with homegrown talent in recent years as they've clung to their aging stars while continually chasing championships.

Jonathan Kuminga is perhaps the biggest example of a failed developmental project. He was drafted in 2021 to a team already competing for titles, giving him little runway to make mistakes.

"No," a Warriors source told Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle when asked whether Kuminga had the chance to fail early in his career. "Not even close. Because we were trying to win titles. And we should be. If you can win a title, you just win a title. F--k development."

Lendeborg started each of his first four games in the NBA while averaging 33.3 minutes. Kuminga was limited to 16.9 minutes per game as a rookie mostly off the bench.

Though Kuminga showed flashes of potential early on, he never panned out the way the Warriors hoped, and they ultimately traded him last season.

Lendeborg figures to be set up for success much more than Kuminga was. While Golden State is still aiming for the playoffs, few expect the Dubs to be Finals contenders. Once Stephen Curry retires, the Warriors will likely be heading towards a full rebuild.

That gives Lendeborg the chance to play big minutes without having the pressure of playing on a championship-caliber team. He's off to a fantastic start, averaging 21.8 points and 9.3 rebounds per game.

articles.title: AJ Dybantsa starts pro career with alley-oop dunk in aggressive, impressive NBA debut
articles.summary: Dybantsa was efficient and aggressive while leading the Wizards in scoring in an NBA debut that was worth the wait.
articles.body:
The Wizards rookie made his delayed debut Wednesday night against the Cleveland Cavaliers after missing Washington's first four games with a sprained ankle. Wizards fans surely liked what they saw.

Dybantsa made an immediate impression off the opening tip and led the Wizards with 19 points.

Dyabntsa immediately sought to make an impact with an aggressive drive to the hole on his first NBA touch off the opening tip. He didn't get the dunk. He did get fouled and hit both free throws for his first NBA points.

There was no stopping Dybantsa on his second dunk attempt.

The athletic 6-foot-9 forward slipped behind the Cleveland defense in transition. Trae Young spotted him from the backcourt and delivered a pass that Dybantsa slammed home from the baseline.

By the end of the first quarter, Dybantsa had nine points on 3-of-3 shooting that included a 3-pointer and a tough floater through traffic.

It was the sort of dynamic offensive display that made Dybantsa college basketball's leading scorer and a first-team All-American as a freshman and the No. 1 pick in the NBA Draft. It helped Washington to a 42-34 first-quarter lead.

While the Wizards ultimately surrendered that lead in a 121-111 Cavaliers win , there was plenty to like from Dybantsa throughout the game.

He added another alley-oop dunk for his first bucket of the second half that prompted the Cavaliers to call timeout.

He finished the game with 19 points, 2 assists and 2 rebounds. He did it on 8-of-12 shooting from the field (1 of 3 from 3) in an impressive display of efficiency in his first game facing regular-season NBA competition.

Playing in a lineup that features multiple-time All-Stars Young and Anthony Davis, Dybantsa was aggressive, but looked for his spots and didn't force his shots. He ended up leading Washington in scoring as Davis and Alex Sarr tallied 18 points each and Young finished with 14. Bilal Coulibaly added 17 points off the bench.

Dybantsa joins a Wizards team featuring veteran All-Stars as an already established star. How he fits into and impacts the lineup as a rookie will be a compelling watch this season as Washington seeks to return to the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

Even though his debut didn't come with a victory, the Wizards are certainly happy with what they saw Wednesday night.

articles.title: AJ Dybantsa Makes Wizards Debut vs. Cavs, Box Score Stats & Highlights for AD, Harden, Top Players
articles.summary: Welcome to the NBA, AJ Dybantsa.
articles.body:
The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 draft made his debut for the Washington Wizards and looked impressive during the team's 121-111 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night.

He reacted to the performance after the game:

Week 1 Grades for Top Stars On New Teams 🌟

Washington wasn't able to emerge victorious after entering the contest as 9.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Here's how key players from the game fared including Dybantsa, Anthony Davis and James Harden:

Dybantsa's 19 points were the most by a Wizards rookie in their debut since 1992 while also being tied for the fourth-most in a debut in team history.

His first career field goal was an impressive one, as he threw down a lob from Trae Young that was tossed from just beyond the halfcourt line.

The 19-year-old repeatedly showcased his athleticism around the rim while also displaying his playmaking potential.

Dybantsa ended up shooting 8-of-12 from the field, including 1-of-3 from three-point territory.

The Wizards put together a high-scoring first quarter, holding a 42-34 lead over the Cavaliers heading into the second.

Washington gained a double-digit advantage early in the second period and didn't look back for the remainder of the first half, maintaining a 69-59 edge at halftime.

The Wizards quickly pushed their lead to 13 points with 10 minutes left in the third, but the Cavs immediately responded with a 23-11 run to keep the game from getting out of hand.

At the end of three quarters, the score was tied 92-92.

Both teams battled to start the fourth before Washington gained a one-point lead with six minutes remaining in the contest, although Cleveland went on another 13-2 run down the stretch of the game to move back in front.

The Wizards were ultimately unable to pull off a late comeback, suffering their third loss of the season to fall to 2-3. The Cavs improved to 3-1 with the victory.

Washington ended the game with a season-high 31 assists as a team, but shot a mere 8-of-32 from three-point territory.

The Wizards are set to host the Charlotte Hornets in their next game on Friday, while the Cavs will travel to face the Atlanta Hawks on Thursday.

articles.title: LeBron, Maxey Lead 76ers' 4Q Comeback vs. Pacers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Top Players
articles.summary: Despite being without Tyrese Haliburton, the Indiana Pacers gave LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey a run for their money on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Despite being without Tyrese Haliburton, the Indiana Pacers gave LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey a run for their money on Wednesday.

The Pacers ultimately came up short against the Philadelphia 76ers, though, losing 114-109 at home after a huge fourth-quarter run led by Maxey.

The Pacers came out of halftime scorching hot, starting the third quarter on a 17-0 run that helped them take the lead. Indiana outscored Philadelphia 36-13 in the third quarter, giving them a 13-point lead heading into the final period.

But after the Pacers' run in the third, the Sixers answered with one of their own in the fourth. Philadelphia went on a 15-2 run to regain the lead halfway through the fourth.

The 76ers' run set up a down-to-the-wire finish.

With Indiana trailing by just two points with a little over a minute to play, Maxey drilled a three-pointer to give Philadelphia some breathing room. Andrew Nembhard drew a foul and hit both free throws to bring the Pacers back within one possession.

But Maxey came through with another clutch basket, making a three off an assist from James to make a 112-106 game.

After Obi Toppin made a free throw to cut the lead to five points, Indiana forced a turnover as the Sixers tried to get the ball up the court with 30 seconds to play. The Pacers couldn't capitalize on the turnover, though, and Philadelphia managed to ice the game at the free-throw line.

The Sixers improved to 4-1 with the win, while the Pacers, who will look to stay afloat without Haliburton for the next few weeks , dropped to 2-3.

articles.title: Naz Reid Benched in 2nd Half of Hornets' Loss to Pistons, HC Explains in Video
articles.summary: Charlotte Hornets head coach Charles Lee discussed the decision to bench forward Naz Reid in the second half of a 97-89 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets head coach Charles Lee discussed the decision to bench forward Naz Reid in the second half of a 97-89 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday.

"Unfortunately, Naz didn't meet our standards in the first half and at halftime we made the decision that he wouldn't play in the second half," Lee told reporters after the game. "But I look forward to him meeting those standards come next game."

Reid played 13 minutes in the first half, scoring seven points and grabbing six rebounds while shooting 2-of-6 from the field. He also recorded one block.

The Hornets led 51-44 at the half, although they were outscored 53-38 over the final two quarters to suffer their second loss of the season.

Reid was replaced in Charlotte's starting lineup by veteran swingman Royce O'Neale to begin the third period. O'Neale scored six points on 2-of-4 shooting in the second half, but didn't record a rebound or assist.

Lee's decision was surprising, as the Hornets acquired Reid as part of the blockbuster trade that sent LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves this summer.

Reid wrapped up an impressive tenure with Minnesota in which he blossomed into a key rotation piece on multiple playoff teams, earning Sixth Man of the Year honors in 2024.

He opened his Hornets career on a high note, as he averaged 19.5 points, 9.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game across his first four games this season. Reid also shot 43.8 percent from the field and 41.2 percent from behind the arc across that span.

Despite his benching on Wednesday, it doesn't appear as though his starting spot is in jeopardy moving forward.

The Hornets will look to bounce back in their next contest, a matchup with the Washington Wizards on Friday. Tip-off is at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Nuggets star Nikola Jokić records 200th career triple-double, rapidly closing in on Russell Westbrook's all-time record
articles.summary: Nikola Jokić is just the second player in NBA history to log 200 triple-doubles in his career.
articles.body:
Nikola Jokić is closing in on Russell Westbrook's triple-double record fast.

The Denver Nuggets star completed the 200th triple-double of his career on Wednesday night while leading them to a 104-91 win over the New Orleans Pelicans. Jokić had 21 points while shooting 8 of 13 from the field at the Smoothie King Center, and he added 13 rebounds and 10 assists. It marked his second triple-double of the season.

Jokić is now just the second player in NBA history with at least 200 triple-doubles in his career. He is just nine away from matching Westbrook's all-time record.

Jokić was already the league's active leader on the triple-double list. Westbrook officially announced his retirement from the NBA in August. He had 209 triple-doubles in his career, and broke Oscar Robertson's all-time record back in 2021. Robertson had 181 in his career.

Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James is the only other active player in the league with triple-digit triple-doubles. He has 125 in his career and is fifth on the all-time list. Magic Johnson had 138 in his career.

The Nuggets led the entire way on Wednesday night. Jamal Murray had 23 points to go with Jokić's triple-double while shooting 5 of 11 from the 3-point line, and Aaron Gordon had 15 points and 11 rebounds. The win moved them to 2-2 on the season.

Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 25 points and five rebounds, and Derik Queen added 11 points and 12 rebounds off the bench. The Pelicans have lost four straight to open the season.

At this rate, it appears to be a matter of time before Jokić breaks Westbrook's record. He had 34 triple-doubles last season alone, and he's up to two through just four games this season.

How far he pushes that record before opting to retire, though, remains to be seen.

articles.title: Los Sixers aprovechan la baja de Haliburton en Indiana
articles.standfirst: Tyrese Maxey fue el mejor de los 76ers con 27 puntos. Embiid (21 puntos y 11 rebotes), Brown (20 puntos y 10 rebotes) y James (13 puntos y 10 asistencias) se llevaron sendos dobles-dobles

articles.body: Los Philadelphia 76ers derrotaron a los Indiana Pacers por 109-114, coincidiendo con la nueva lesión de Tyrese Haliburton, que estará al menos dos semanas de baja por una lesión en los isquiotibiales. Haliburton, fuera de las pistas toda la temporada pasada por una rotura del Aquiles, había jugado los cuatro primeros partidos de esta campaña, en los que promedió 21,3 puntos y 9,5 asistencias, antes de volver a quedar fuera de las pistas por lesión. Sin Haliburton enfrente, los 76ers de LeBron James, Jaylen Brown o Joel Embiid se pusieron rápidamente con una ventaja de 15 en el segundo cuarto, que cerraron con un espectacular triple de VJ Edgecombe sobre la bocina desde su propia cancha. Pero los Pacers abrieron el segundo tiempo con un parcial de 17-0, cortado con un triple de James, con el que se pusieron por delante hasta terminar el tercer cuarto con un +13. Sin embargo, el oficio de los hombres de Nick Nurse se impuso en el tramo final, cuando James y compañía retomaron la ventaja y se llevaron un duelo más reñido de lo esperado. Tyrese Maxey fue el mejor de los 76ers con 27 puntos. Embiid (21 puntos y 11 rebotes), Brown (20 puntos y 10 rebotes) y James (13 puntos y 10 asistencias) se llevaron sendos dobles-dobles de Indianápolis. Anfernee Simons aportó otros 20 puntos. Para los Pacers, Pascal Siakam terminó con 26 puntos y 11 rebotes, Andrew Nembhard con 18 puntos y 14 asistencias y Aaron Nesmith otros 18 puntos. Kelly Oubre Jr. terminó con 15 puntos en su primer duelo contra su exequipo. Con esta victoria, los 76ers se sitúan en lo más alto del Este, con un balance de 4-1, mientras que los Pacers quedan con un registro de 2-3

articles.summary: Dybantsa, de 19 años, se perdió los cuatro primeros partidos de la temporada por un esguince de tobillo

Dybantsa, de 19 años, se perdió los cuatro primeros partidos de la temporada por un esguince de tobillo sufrido durante la pretemporada. articles.summary: Jokic cerró el partido con 23 puntos, 13 rebotes y 10 asistencias en el triunfo de sus Denver Nuggets en Nueva Orleans
articles.body: El serbio Nikola Jokic firmó su triple-doble número 200 en la NBA ante los New Orleans Pelicans, a sólo nueve del récord absoluto de 209 que tiene Russell Westbrook. El tercero, relegado con 181, es el legendario Oscar Robertson.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Denies Celtics Trade Request amid Rumors, Sounds Off on 'False Allegations' in Video
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown is setting the record straight.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown is setting the record straight.

The Philadelphia 76ers star was asked about a report from Boston Celtics color commentator and former player Brian Scalabrine suggesting he requested a trade away from the Celtics.

"I love Scal, but I guess he's doing what he has to do. I can understand why he feels the need to do that," Brown told reporters Wednesday. "But I have no interest in letting any false allegations follow me to my next chapter here in Philadelphia. I never demanded a trade, never made a list of ultimatums. Nothing of the sort."

USA Today's Celtics Wire noted Scalabrine walked back some of his initial reporting when he addressed the situation on NBC Sports Boston on Monday, adding "he technically didn't demand any trade."

Brown was definitive in his comments Wednesday and made it seem like he is ready to move on from any speculation and embrace his opportunity to chase a championship with the 76ers.

Boston ended up trading him to Philadelphia in a move that brought Paul George back to the Celtics, and the early returns have worked out well for the 76ers. They improved to 4-1 with Wednesday's 114-109 comeback win over the Indiana Pacers.

Brown posted a double-double of 20 points, 10 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block behind 7-of-13 shooting from the field.

If he can find a way to impact the game in a number of ways like that while playing alongside plenty of star power in Tyrese Maxey, LeBron James and Joel Embiid, the 76ers will be a daunting opponent for the entire Eastern Conference.

Brown won a championship with the Celtics and is looking to add another one in Philadelphia after shutting down some of what he called "false allegations" that have generated attention in the early going this season.

articles.title: Jr. NBA shifts focus to under-16s, with year-round play and better coaching key to developing Indian talent
articles.summary: When some of India's best school-level basketball talent returned from the Rising Stars Invitational in Singapore earlier this year, Sunny Malik asked
articles.body: When some of India's best school-level basketball talent returned from the Rising Stars Invitational in Singapore earlier this year, Sunny Malik asked them what they had learnt from the tournament. Their answer was straightforward. They had struggled to keep pace as the game wore on, and their stamina and endurance needed work.“They said that the level of competition showed us that we need to improve a lot more. We ended up lacking in stamina and endurance. That’s what those kids told me,” Malik, NBA India Country Head, told TimesofIndia.com on the sidelines of ACG Jr. NBA 3v3 National Tournament in Delhi last week.“Imagine the kind of learning that they have through that one game stating that by third quarter we were lot of losing it and fourth quarter we were down.”The players were already looking ahead to the next edition. They told Malik they would work on those weaknesses before returning to Singapore.“They said that if we are the best team in India next year and we participate in RSI next year, we assure you that we will go to at least semis. Because we will work on our stamina, we will work on our endurance and we will work on the weaknesses that we saw through the entire program,” he said.“That is what we want kids to know.”Malik returned to that experience while discussing the ACG Jr. NBA 3v3 National Tournament, where teams from schools with established basketball programmes competed alongside those from schools without the same infrastructure.The 2026 edition has moved from the under-14 to the under-16 category. The 10-city competition began in September and will culminate in national finals in December.Delhi recorded 270 team registrations across 118 schools: 193 boys’ teams and 77 girls’ teams.For Malik, the tournament is an opportunity for players to discover the standard of competition beyond their own schools and assess what it takes to keep up.“The overall exposure and learning that they can get through this program, playing against the best teams coming in from a city or the outskirts of that city, is the main objective is,” he said.Better strategy over physical prowessDuring a girls’ game in Delhi, the difference in positioning was evident. In the half-court format, with 12 seconds to attack, one team struggled to find its positions while the other exploited the gaps. Malik, responding to the observation, said the difference was down to strategy rather than size.“Somewhere these kids are playing better because they are not bigger than their opposition; they [opposition] are playing better because their strategy is better,” Malik said.He sees that contrast between schools that have a structured basketball programme and those where children learn largely through experience. “And that's where I see the difference between a school having a basketball program and school not having a basketball program because, you know, then they are running ad hoc, wanting to work not through a strategy but through their individual learning,” he said.“Whereas a school having a basketball program teaches you about this positioning, how do you pass, how do you ensure that you are able to score a bucket in that time that you have got.”The technical side of the game is only one part of what young players need to develop. Malik said the Singapore experience had also brought the physical and mental demands of international competition into focus.“Personally, when I saw a lot of these teams playing at RSI, I felt the one thing that a lot of our teams have to work on is endurance, stamina building, mental conditioning,” he said.“Playing against the best in the world requires that toughness, that endurance, that you will continue for those four quarters at your peak.”Malik wants greater investment in coachesThe Singapore experience also sharpened Malik’s view of what needs attention away from competition. He believes coaching development is one area of Indian sport that still requires more investment.“Coaches development is one area which probably, and that's my personal take, gets ignored sometimes,” he said. “But that's a very, very important part of the overall ecosystem development.”“Unless you invest in coaches, unless you support coaches with a training level which is world class, how do those coaches produce world-class talent? So investment in coaching, infra coaching ecosystem is an important part that every organisation should look into which is invested in sports. Only then can you produce world-class athletes from that.”The Jr. NBA programme has been running in India since 2013, reaching more than 15 million young people and 15,000 physical education instructors across 35 cities.International coaches, including Natalia André, have been involved in coaching clinics and development work across the region. But Malik acknowledged the limits of a programme that moves between cities over a few days.“That's challenging. If it's a five-day program in the city, the best that you can do is train some of the coaches,” he said.“The best that you can do is, if you genuinely see some talent, you can sit with them, spend some time and explain them that where were they lacking so that they take those learning out of coaches like Natalia who is coming from outside world and seeing the best kids playing in the APAC or across the globe.”The work with coaches is intended to continue after the tournament teams leave. Malik said the programme had used coaching clinics to introduce local instructors to the curriculum and standards followed by international coaches.“Through the global coaches that we have, coaching clinics with them, trying to tell them what the right level of coaching is, what kind of curriculum do we follow,” he said.He put the responsibility on those coaches to keep children playing once the tournament window closes. “The objective is that participation should not stop once the program gets over,” Malik said.“So if it's a four-month program, you don't want kids to only play for four months. You want them to play through the year. And for that, these coaches have to play an important role in conditioning them, welding on the learnings that they have drawn through this competition, and then improving on those.”Malik said the coaching ecosystem had improved, but still needed support and investment if India was to produce world-class players.More girls are playing; the league question remainsThe Delhi numbers also reflect a broader feature of the Jr. NBA programme: girls’ participation. Malik said some city-level competitions had recorded girls’ participation of around 40-45%, a figure he found encouraging.“I personally don't see a lot of sports where girls participation is as high as 45% in a city-level competition,” he said.“So, girls participation at 40-45% encourages us a lot that through this program you are also bringing in girls into the mainstream of sports. And that's one of the big objectives that we have.”The tournament’s national finals are another step for teams that progress through the city competitions. After holding the finals in Delhi for the previous two years, organisers intend to stage this year’s event in Chennai.Malik said changing the venue would give players experience of competing in a different city and arena. “Because if these kids have to play at national level, they will be, you know, going across the country. You don't want to just stay to one location,” he said.“Similarly, ACG Junior NBA finals across different cities would always, you know, be helpful for these kids who are getting into a final. They are getting into more exposure into a different city, different environment, different arena, different exposure.”The top two boys’ teams and top two girls’ teams from each city, along with selected all-star teams, are set to qualify for the December finals.Whether the competition can help players move towards professional basketball is a separate question. A proposed Indian basketball league could provide another platform. For Malik, though, its talent-identification process would become clearer as the plans take shape.“I think anything which helps basketball in the country, NBA would always be the first one to support that initiative. We would love to support any initiative which gets kids the pathway that they are looking at,” he said.“Getting kids the pathway, getting kids the right platform to showcase their talent is a great initiative. We are definitely in support of anything which helps basketball in the country.”He also wants the sport to attract a wider audience. “As a category, it's important for basketball to become prime time. As a category, it's important for people to watch, people to play, people to participate. We are in support of any initiative helping basketball.”Asked whether players in the under-16 tournament could progress into the proposed league, Malik said he was not privy to its structure or the plans of its coaches and scouts.He did, however, point to the existing partnership between ACG and the Jr. NBA programme, saying players who performed well could come to the attention of organisations looking for talent.“Some of these talents, which would do well at these levels, would automatically form a part of the larger talent pool, which would be visible to everyone,” he said.The under-16 tournament offers a competitive platform, but what happens after December will depend in part on whether players continue to train and compete. Malik’s expectation is clear: the four-month programme should not be the only time they play.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Yaxel Lendeborg 'Absolutely' Ready for Luka Rematch After Warriors Rookie Ripped Lakers Star
articles.summary: In his first NBA game, Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg got into it with Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić.
articles.body:
In his first NBA game, Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg got into it with Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić.

The two exchanged trash talk throughout the game, and Lendeborg never backed down despite Dončić's status as a veteran. The Warriors and Lakers will face each other again on Friday, and Lendeborg can't wait.

"Absolutely. Absolutely. Yes, I am," he told reporters. "I'll talk about that on Friday."

Insider Explains Yaxel vs. Kuminga Opportunity

Despite it being his NBA debut, Lendeborg was quick to talk trash to Dončić and even earned a technical foul.

The former Michigan star then called out Dončić after the game, saying that he "lost all respect" for him because he was "complaining the entire game." Lendeborg also said that he told Dončić that "he sucks."

Dončić obviously has a much more impressive resume than Lendeborg, but clearly isn't going to stop the rookie from going after him.

Lendeborg, the No. 11 overall pick, has looked like an early candidate for Rookie of the Year so far. He's averaging 21.8 points and 9.3 rebounds per game, having dropped 31 points on Monday before posting 26 against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday.

He'll look to have the best game of his young career against Dončić and the Lakers on Friday.

articles.title: Lakers rout Clippers 103-87 without Luka Doncic
articles.summary: (AP) — Quentin Grimes scored 23 points, Collin Sexton added a season-high 21 points off the bench, and the Los Angeles Lakers — without Luka Doncic — beat th...
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — Quentin Grimes scored 23 points, Collin Sexton added a season-high 21 points off the bench, and the Los Angeles Lakers — without Luka Doncic — beat the Los Angeles Clippers 103-87 on Wednesday night for the second time in a week.

Doncic sat out with back tightness from the second game of the team's first back-to-back of the season. Starting forward Ziaire Williams missed the game with a sore left foot. Coach JJ Redick said both moves were precautionary.

Without Doncic's NBA-leading 36-point average, the Lakers (4-1) had six players in double figures. Austin Reaves had 16 points and Matisse Thybulle had 15. Sexton and Thybulle had four 3-pointers each.

Rookie Keaton Wagler scored a career-high 21 points off the bench to lead the Clippers (1-3). They dropped their third in a row, having lost to the Lakers by eight points on Friday. They were without starting forward Rui Hachimura (left quad tightness) against his former team.

The Clippers again failed to hold onto the ball with 24 turnovers. They had 26 in each of their last two games, both losses to the Thunder and Lakers.

Down 18 points, the Clippers briefly rallied to open the third, outscoring the Lakers 12-2 to pull within seven. But the Lakers closed the quarter on a 27-15 spurt, with Sexton reeling off 11 consecutive points including back-to-back 3-pointers for an 85-65 lead.

The Lakers took control in the second quarter, outscoring the Clippers 31-6, including 16 points in a row, to take a 56-38 halftime lead. Six different players scored for the Lakers, led by Reaves with nine.

Lakers: At Golden State on Friday night to open NBA Cup group play.

Clippers: At Minnesota on Friday night to open NBA Cup group play.

After Brandin Podziemski and the Golden State Warriors beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 119-114, the third-year guard revealed he's been watching New York Knicks All-Star Jalen Brunson 's tape. Podziemski missed the Warriors' regular-season opener due to a back injury, but has been looking to find his stride amidst Golden State's first two weeks of the regular season.

Ahead of the regular season, Podziemski says he spent the offseason studying Brunson's approach, per NBC Sports Bay Area.

"Watching film. I watched a lot of Brunson tape this summer, understanding that guys who make jumps in this league shoot a lot more threes, a lot more free throws. And the back half of last season, that's what I did, and I'm just trying to continue that," Podziemski said. "I know our team notoriously doesn't get fouled a lot, and shoot a lot of free throws. So, for me, if I'm able to do that, reset a possession, and slow the game down a little bit, get the legs back under us; that's what we need."

Golden State Warriors forward Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely as he is dealing with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), a condition that affects an individual's heart rate and blood pressure.

Porzingis has not played this season. He signed a two-year, $40 million contract extension with the Warriors in the summer.

The 31-year-old star has missed plenty of games throughout his career due to various ailments. Amid his POTS and uncertain future, he flew to Spain for dental work , according to NBA Central.

Unable to do any basketball activity, Porzingis is trying to carry on with his personal life.

Still, his trip drew the ire of fans, especially in Golden State.

"Getting veneers instead of rebounds," said @kkentrell5.

"Yeah, this MF ain't stepping foot on the court anytime soon. His a** is out here doing side quests and s***, LMAO," added @LONDO87540615.

Before the season, he was optimistic about helping the Warriors and having a full campaign with Stephen Curry and Draymond Green. But alas, Porzingis suffered another setback , prompting him to seriously consider retirement.

articles.title: Why Knicks Benched Mikal Bridges With No Injury
articles.summary: The New York Knicks are searching. They have yet to replicate their NBA championship form so far in the new season. Mikal Bridges has been a bit part of the...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are searching. They have yet to replicate their NBA championship form so far in the new season.

Mikal Bridges has been a bit part of the struggles, and that came to a head on Wednesday night in Chicago against the Bulls. Bridges appears to have gotten benched, at least temporarily.

The Knicks subbed Bridges out with 8:09 left in the third quarter, and he didn't play the rest of the frame or into the start of the fourth quarter.

Barring a late change, that may have been Bridges' last action of the night.

Up to that 8:09 mark of the third quarter, Bridges had played 13 minutes. He had three points on 1-for-4 shooting from the field, including 1-for-2 from 3-point range.

Bridges had yet to record a rebound, or an assist, or a steal, or a block. He had one turnover and was a minus-5.

The Knicks can't be happy with Bridges' play so far this season.

His non-impact 13 minutes on Wednesday night were just a continuation of what he's done already this season — or more accurately, has not done.

Bridges' season game log before Thursday looked like this:

12 points, 3 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 steal

He has begun the year shooting just 9-for-33 from the floor (27.3%) and 4-for-18 from 3-point range (22.2%). That's simply not good enough for a player who isn't known as a great rebounder or passer.

Bridges is an impactful defender when he's dialed in, so that's the one thing the Knicks really risk losing by not playing him.

But given that the Knicks had begun the season just 1-3 and were then in a dogfight with the Bulls on Wednesday night, head coach Mike Brown must've felt it was time to shake something up. Bridges won't be benched permanently, but a bit of an extended gap without him in the rotation was meant to force the Knicks to do something differently.

Does Mikal Bridges Get Voided on DraftKings, FanDuel?

The major sportsbooks have injury protection for NBA players, but Bridges doesn't appear to qualify.

For one, he did play four minutes in the second half, and a lot of the policies depend on something happening in the first half.

And two, Bridges wasn't injured, unless the Knicks say differently postgame. He seems simply to have been benched.

It might just be a bad break for anyone who was counting on Bridges on Wednesday night.

articles.title: Yaxel Lendeborg is ready to reignite his newfound rivalry with Luka Doncic
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg is just a few games into his career, but he already has a prominent rivalry with a true superstar.
articles.body:
To start the 2026-27 NBA season, Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg ignited a rivalry with Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Doncic. It was a big story because Lendeborg was not shy about talking trash to one of the league's best players.

Since that was his first-ever NBA game, it was even more impressive. Lendeborg has never been the type of player to back down from a challenge, and that has led to him playing so well in his rookie year so far. Now, he has another shot at Doncic, and it could be a golden opportunity.

Yaxel Lendeborg wants to keep challenging Luka Doncic

Doncic has been one of the best players in the league yet again this season. He is fresh off games where he scored 50+ points and 40+ points, which is a bad sign for anyone who wants to defend him.

On Friday, the Lakers and the Warriors will play against each other again. While Doncic had 28 points during their first matchup, Lendeborg did hold him to some inefficient numbers when he was matched up against him.

Since that game, Lendeborg has also been superb to start his NBA career. In his first five games, Lendeborg has averaged 22.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, and four assists per game. He definitely has shown that he is ready for the big leagues, and that involves him playing against stars like Doncic.

"Absolutely. Yes, I am. I'll talk about that on Friday," Lendeborg said in response to a question about his matchup against Doncic on Friday .

Lendeborg is certainly a breath of fresh air because he is quite vocal as a rookie. Most first-year players are reserved because they are just entering the league, so they don't want to ruffle any feathers.

That is not the case with Lendeborg, who is quite older than his fellow 2026 draftees. However, Lendeborg does have the personality to match the words that he has said over the past few weeks.

articles.title: ‘It’s Still Hard, Brother’ — Charles Barkley Fights Back Emotions While Reacting to Ernie Johnson’s Retirement News
articles.summary: Charles Barkley struggled to hold back tears as he addressed Ernie Johnson’s decision to step away from “Inside the NBA” after the 2026-27 season. The Hall o...
articles.body:
Charles Barkley struggled to hold back tears as he addressed Ernie Johnson's decision to step away from "Inside the NBA" after the 2026-27 season.

The Hall of Famer has spent more than two decades alongside Johnson, and he wasn't the only panelist moved by the announcement.

Charles Barkley Gets Emotional After Ernie Johnson's Major Announcement

Johnson, who has hosted "Inside the NBA" since 1990, announced Wednesday on social media that he will leave the show at the end of the season, concluding a 37-year run. His departure will mark the first major change to the show's longtime lineup in years.

Barkley addressed the news alongside fellow panelists Shaquille O'Neal and Kenny Smith, reflecting on the years he has spent with the legendary studio host.

"That was tough," Barkley admitted. "We knew the day was coming. It's still tough. I've been here 26, 27 years, and it's been an honor and a privilege to work with you all this time."

"Even though I knew this was coming, it's still hard, brother," the former NBA MVP added , describing Johnson as the "leader" of their group.

Barkley joined "Inside the NBA" in 2000, becoming a regular presence alongside Johnson and Smith. O'Neal joined the panel in 2011, completing the quartet that has since become one of television's most recognizable broadcasting teams.

Over the years, the four have developed a chemistry built around their contrasting personalities, with Johnson often guiding discussions as Barkley, Smith, and O'Neal debate games, players, and league developments. Their exchanges have become a regular part of NBA coverage beyond the games themselves.

Smith compared working with Johnson to entering the Houston Rockets' locker room for the first time. The two-time NBA champion credited the veteran broadcaster's energy for giving him the belief that their group could accomplish something special.

O'Neal, meanwhile, said the chance to work with Johnson helped persuade him to join "Inside the NBA."

In his announcement, Johnson revealed that he has dealt with "heart issues" over the past two years. Although his doctor had not advised him to step away, the longtime host said he wanted to spend more time with his family. His decision comes after decades of balancing a demanding broadcasting schedule with his personal life.

The veteran sportscaster also clarified that he is not retiring from broadcasting entirely. He plans to continue covering March Madness and pursuing other television projects, while his new production company, "32 Bowties," will focus on telling "feel-good stories" in sports.

Johnson will continue hosting "Inside the NBA" through the 2026-27 campaign before stepping away from the show.

articles.title: Knicks Notes: Jalen Brunson and the offense beginning to emerge; Tyler Kolek impressing
articles.summary: After a slow start, Jalen Brunson and his Knicks teammates certainly kept shooting - and shooting well - on Wednesday night against the Chicago Bulls.
articles.body:
Knicks star Jalen Brunson didn't shoot well in the first four games of the season. He also didn't shoot well in the first four minutes of Wednesday's game in Chicago.

He missed three of his first four shots against the Bulls. At that moment, he was shooting 36 percent (31-for-86) on the season and 19 percent (4-for-21) from beyond the arc.

If you were getting a little antsy in the opening minutes on Wednesday, Brunson probably put you at ease over the course of the night.

The 2026 NBA Finals MVP hit six of his next nine three-pointers (12-for-21 overall) to help New York rebound from a 19-point third quarter deficit and take the second game of a back-to-back .

He finished with a season-high 38 points, seven assists, and two steals in New York's first road win of the year.

The Knicks shot a season-high 46 percent from three and 45 percent overall in the comeback win.

They looked like the potent offense that emerged late last regular season and then again in Game 4 of their first-round series win over the Hawks.

For what it's worth, Mike Brown was not panicked at all about his team's shooting.

"The biggest thing is: are we getting good shots from the right people? Watching the film and watching the game, I think we are," Brown said before the Knicks' win over Detroit on Tuesday. "We've had some pretty good looks from the right people at the right time that normally go in so I want them to keep shooting."

After a slow start, Brunson and his teammates certainly kept shooting - and shooting well - on Wednesday night.

The difference for New York in the past two games has been taking care of the minor details on both ends of the floor.

"(We've got to) focus on the little things until we get our rhythm. Once we get a rhythm, continue to do the little things. It' a big point of emphasis right no, our attention to detail."

They executed enough of the little things and big things to leave Chicago with a win. Next up? Friday night in Philadelphia.

If you see a lineup this season that you haven't seen the last two years, don't get alarmed. That's Mike Brown's way of stress-testing some ideas.

"There's some things that I'm looking at or messing with that may or may not stay the same," Brown said. "That's part of what you're trying to do to figure out what's best for your team long term."

One example? Brown played lineups with Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns on the bench in the first two games. Brown abandoned that idea. But don't be surprised if you see a few non-traditional lineups over the next couple of weeks as Brown gets a feel for this year's version of the team.

Tyler Kolek has move the ball well during Jose Alvarado 's absence.

Alvarado missed his third straight game due to an ankle injury. Kolek played well, finishing with nine assists and zero turnovers. He has 21 assists and zero turnovers over the last three games. If you're wondering what Brown expects of Kolek, the coach laid it all out on Tuesday:

"He's gotta run the team. What I mean by that is, when you watch our games, when he goes on the floor, people get up into his chest when he's trying to run our offense. He can't get off the ball too early, if it's just one guy," Brown explained. "He's gotta be able to go by that guy and get the guy off-balance and bring it back out and set our offense up and/or get by and make a play in the paint. He can't let pressure bother him or disrupt our offense at all.

"And then defensively, he's gotta be a pest. He's gotta be nasty, not anything illegal or anything like that, just a guy that people wanna say 'get off me, get off me,' because he's more than capable of doing that. He's gotta play with some sort of force, particularly for his size."

Whether or not Kolek checked those boxes is open to interpretation. But, objectively speaking, Kolek has made some great reads with the ball - and protected it.

Kolek wasn't the only Knick to thrive off the bench Wednesday. Landry Shamet and Jordan Clarkson combined for 32 points on 12-for-21 shooting. New York outscored Chicago by 13 with either Shamet or Clarkson on the floor Wednesday.

articles.title: ‘He feels terrible’: Steve Kerr says why Yaxel Lendeborg is ‘not happy at all’ despite Warriors win
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr has claimed that Yaxel Lendeborg was not happy with his performance against the Minnesota Timberwolves. The Warri...
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr has claimed that Yaxel Lendeborg was not happy with his performance against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Warriors have now won back-to-back games after starting the season with three consecutive losses. Their season looks to be back on track now, and Lendeborg has definitely played his part.

Even against the Timberwolves, the 24-year-old produced a number of outstanding moments, but there were a few others that showed he needs to improve.

Steve Kerr says Yaxel Lendeborg was feeling 'terrible' in the locker room

Lendeborg recorded 26 points and eight rebounds in 35 minutes for the Warriors in their 119-114 win over the Timberwolves on Wednesday night.

Usually, such a return is rewarded with a lot of praise, and he would be the hero in the locker room after the game. But that was not the case.

That's because Lendeborg committed seven turnovers in the game, which he knows is not good enough at this level. He just can't be doing that.

That is why he was devastated in the locker room after the game, despite all the other positives.

Kerr said in his press conference : "We just show him the film and get him to understand time and score. The general idea is, if you have an advantage, take it. If you don't, don't try to force it. And he tried to force a bunch of plays tonight.

"It's his fifth game in the NBA. So, I'm really excited. I'm almost glad that's happened. So, he feels it. He feels terrible in there. He's not happy at all.

"And yet, he had 26 points and eight boards in his fifth NBA game. So, it's a great lesson for him. The simple play is the best one, over and over and over again.

"And we have enough guys already on this team who are going to turn it over. So he needs to be solid. He needs to learn the value of just making the simple play."

Lendeborg not being happy with the turnovers he conceded in a game where he scored 26 points to help his side win speaks volumes about his mentality.

It would be easy to ignore the negatives and just focus on the positives, but the fact that he was so upset shows he has the perfect mentality.

However, as Kerr said, he's only five games into his NBA career, so we're sure moments like these will help him, not hurt him.

articles.title: Los Lakers, sin Doncic, se pasean por Inglewood
articles.standfirst: El español Baba Miller sumó 4 puntos, 7 rebotes (mejor reboteador de su equipo), 1 asistencia, 1 robo y 2 tapones.
articles.summary: El español Baba Miller sumó 4 puntos, 7 rebotes (mejor reboteador de su equipo), 1 asistencia, 1 robo y 2 tapones.
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers se llevaron el derbi de Los Ángeles al imponerse por 87-103 a los Clippers, en un partido que afrontaron sin Luka Doncic, baja por unas molestias en la espalda. Los Lakers venían de jugar el martes en Portland, donde encajaron su primera derrota de la temporada. Doncic, autor de 41 puntos contra los Trail Blazers, se levantó esta mañana con dolor en la espalda, según la franquicia. Una baja por precaución que no debería impedirle disputar los próximos partidos. Sin Doncic, los Lakers salieron con un quinteto formado por Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Jake LaRavia y Matisse Thybulle. Un parcial de 0-16 en el segundo cuarto, que llevó el marcador del 31-29 al 31-45, permitió a los Lakers abrir una brecha que ya no volvieron a ver amenazada en un partido muy cómodo para los hombres de JJ Redick. Quentin Grimes fue el máximo anotador oro y púrpura con 23 puntos, mientras que Collin Sexton, suplente, firmó 21. Austin Reaves terminó con 16 tras quedarse en blanco todo el segundo tiempo. Para los Clippers, su mejor jugador fue el 'rookie' y suplente Keaton Wagler con 21 puntos. Derrick Jones Jr. terminó con 15 y Darius Garland con 14. El español Baba Miller disputó 17 minutos con los Clippers, en los que pudo sumar 4 puntos (2 de 3 en tiros de campo), 7 rebotes (mejor reboteador de su equipo), 1 asistencia, 1 robo y 2 tapones. Los Lakers presentan un balance de cuatro victorias y una derrota en sus cinco primeros partidos de la temporada, mientras que los Clippers solo han ganado uno de sus cuatro encuentros.
